description: Parameters needed to the corresponding task specification in eTaSL

from-force_control_task_lib-version-1.0..description:
Library force_control_task_lib version 1.0.1.
 Set to true to indicate that task specification comes from the library above. 
 Library description: Library with eTaSL task specifications for force control tasks for Crospi
Authors: Santiago Iregui (KU Leuven), Erwin Aertbeliën (KU Leuven), Federico Ulloa (KU Leuven)

is-move_admittance.description:
Task Specification: move_admittance.etasl.lua
Set to true to indicate that the task uses the task specification mentioned above. 
 Task description: Admittance control: the robot is compliant to external forces and torques measured by a force/torque sensor, e.g. to guide it by hand. Along each axis of task_frame the robot moves with a velocity proportional to the external force: K_force*F/K_t [m/s] for translations (if activate_linear) and K_torque*T/K_r [rad/s] for rotations (if activate_angular); i.e. it behaves as a damper with damping K_t/K_force [Ns/m] and K_r/K_torque [Nms/rad] and does not return to its initial pose. Non-activated motions keep their initial value. The measured wrench is read from the input channel named by wrench_input_channel (default "wrench_input") (type wrench, expressed in FT_sensor_frame with its origin as reference point), provided by the robot driver/simulator (e.g. MuJoCo) or by a WrenchInputHandler; it is converted to the wrench acting on the robot (see wrench_convention), passed through a dead zone, compensated for the tool weight and expressed in task_frame with its origin as reference point. The task has no monitor: it runs until it is stopped from outside. Outputs: time, position of task_frame (x_tcp, y_tcp, z_tcp), its pose (tf) and the raw input force (x_force, y_force, z_force, as received on wrench_input).
Gravity compensation (tool_weight > 0): it assumes that the force/torque sensor was tared with the tool completely vertical, pointing down (the z axis of FT_sensor_frame along gravity, -z of the robot base frame); the tool weight measured in other orientations of the tool is then compensated.

file_path.description: File path of the corresponding task specification

parameters.description: List of parameters needed to define an instance of the task specification

FT_sensor_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (from the robot model) of the force/torque sensor. The measured wrench of the input channel (wrench_input_channel) is expressed in this frame, with its origin as reference point

K_r.description: Rotational stiffness [Nm/rad] used as model of the admittance around the x, y and z axes of task_frame: the angular velocity is K_torque*T/K_r, with T the external torque [Nm] w.r.t. the origin of task_frame. Higher values make the robot rotate slower for the same torque; lower values make it more compliant. Must be positive. Only used if activate_angular is true

tool_COG.description: Position [m] of the center of gravity of the tool (everything mounted after the force/torque sensor), as [x,y,z] expressed in FT_sensor_frame. Used for the gravity compensation together with tool_weight

task_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (from the robot model) that is controlled, e.g. the tool center point. The admittance is applied along/around its axes and the torques are taken w.r.t. its origin

activate_angular.description: If true, the rotations of task_frame are compliant to the external torques (admittance with K_r). If false, the orientation of task_frame is kept at its initial value

weight_keep_position.description: Weight [-] of the constraint that keeps the initial position of task_frame (activate_linear false) relative to the other constraints of the same priority

K_force.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the translational admittance constraints (activate_linear true): the velocity is K_force*F/K_t. Higher values make the robot move faster for the same force

tool_weight.description: Weight [N] (gravity force, not mass) of the tool mounted after the force/torque sensor, applied at tool_COG, with gravity along -z of the robot base frame. The gravity compensation assumes that the force/torque sensor was tared with the tool completely vertical, pointing down (the z axis of FT_sensor_frame along gravity): it removes the change of the tool weight measured by the sensor when the tool is in another orientation. 0 disables the gravity compensation (e.g. when the tool weight is negligible, or the simulator does not measure it)

force_threshold.description: Dead zone [N] applied to each force component of the measured wrench (in FT_sensor_frame): components with an absolute value below it are set to zero and larger ones are reduced by it. It avoids drift due to sensor noise and offsets. 0 disables the dead zone

K_keep_position.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the constraint that keeps the initial position of task_frame when activate_linear is false. Higher values correct deviations faster

weight_torque.description: Weight [-] of the rotational admittance constraints relative to the other constraints of the same priority. Only matters when the constraints conflict

K_torque.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the rotational admittance constraints (activate_angular true): the angular velocity is K_torque*T/K_r. Higher values make the robot rotate faster for the same torque

torque_threshold.description: Dead zone [Nm] applied to each torque component of the measured wrench (in FT_sensor_frame): components with an absolute value below it are set to zero and larger ones are reduced by it. 0 disables the dead zone

weight_force.description: Weight [-] of the translational admittance constraints relative to the other constraints of the same priority. Only matters when the constraints conflict

wrench_convention.description: Sign convention of the wrench received on the input channel (wrench_input_channel). exerted_on_environment: it is the wrench that the robot exerts on the environment (e.g. the MuJoCo simulator); it is negated to obtain the wrench acting on the robot. exerted_on_robot: it is the wrench that the environment (e.g. a person guiding the robot) exerts on the robot and is used as is. The robot moves along the wrench acting on it

activate_linear.description: If true, the translations of task_frame are compliant to the external forces (admittance with K_t). If false, the position of task_frame is kept at its initial value

wrench_input_channel.description: Name of the input channel (type wrench) from which the measured wrench of the force/torque sensor is read: the varname of the input handler that provides it (e.g. a WrenchInputHandler), or the channel fed directly by the robot driver/simulator (name_expr_cartesian_wrench of the MuJoCo simulator). Change it to use another sensor or input handler

weight_keep_orientation.description: Weight [-] of the constraint that keeps the initial orientation of task_frame (activate_angular false) relative to the other constraints of the same priority

K_keep_orientation.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the constraint that keeps the initial orientation of task_frame when activate_angular is false. Higher values correct deviations faster

K_t.description: Translational stiffness [N/m] used as model of the admittance along the x, y and z axes of task_frame: the velocity is K_force*F/K_t, with F the external force [N]. Higher values make the robot move slower for the same force (it feels heavier); lower values make it more compliant. Must be positive
